_comment: UC-PB-03 Goal Builder. On most characters' numbers a goal takes longer than the twelve months the LifePath covers, so the year-one milestone is written as the normal, respectable outcome — not as failure.
hook: You know what you are saving for. Now work out when you actually get it.
summary: Your goal has a number and a date now.

predict.question: Guess first: saving {monthly} a month, how many months until you have {amount}?
predict.off: Not quite. It is {actual} months. The gap between what we guess and what the maths says is the whole reason to write it down.

plan.how_much: How much can you put away each month?
plan.reached_in: At {monthly} a month, you get there in {count} months.
plan.reached_by: At {monthly} a month, you get there by {festival}.
plan.reached_next_year: At {monthly} a month, you get there by {festival} next year.
plan.never: At nothing a month, this never arrives. Try moving the slider.
plan.year_one: Twelve months from now you will have {amount} — that is {percent}% of the way there.
plan.long_goal: This is a goal bigger than one year. That is normal, and it is not a reason to pick a smaller dream. Aim at the twelve-month mark and keep going.

specific.title: Which one, exactly?
specific.why: A goal with a number and a name is one you can actually hit. “Some money saved” is not a goal.

phone.refurb: A refurbished phone that works fine

bike.used: A used bike in good condition

concept.goal: A goal needs three things: what it is, how much it costs, and the month you expect to have it.
